summary: Multipart request with attachments loses model pin during edge normalization canary
description: Issue summary: After the new edge header normalization service was rolled out to a small canary cohort, certain customer requests that include multipart bodies (text + file attachment) are being routed to a default/legacy model variant instead of the customer's pinned model. Impact: Cartograph Labs reports inconsistent responses for ~2% of inference requests since 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC, producing unexpected formatting and occasional tokenization differences. This affects live user traffic on dedicated deployment and causes degraded model correctness for affected sessions. Environment: production (dedicated tenancy), us-east region, edge normalization canary enabled on a subset of edge nodes.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer tenant Cartograph Labs with a pinned model rw-13b-v1.
2) Send an API request that uses multipart/form-data: a small prompt field + a binary attachment (~50KB image) in the same request payload.
3) Repeat the request several times from the same session; observe that ~1 in 50 requests are served by a fallback model variant (rw-7b-quant) with different tokenization and output format.
4) Re-run the same tests via a non-canary edge node or with canary disabled and confirm consistent pin retention.
logs: Edge-proxy request traces show header set: 'X-Edge-Norm: applied' for affected requests.
Routing decision log excerpt: tenant_pin=null -> route=default-variant (timestamp 2026-03-12T08:14:22Z).
Serving runtime returned model id rw-7b-quant for request id req-8493021 (Cartograph Labs).
No errors returned to client (200 OK), only model output differs.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: header rewrite during normalization strips or mutates the tenant pin header used by the routing mesh for multipart requests.
Edge-proxy team reproduced locally: multipart parsing path triggers a different header injection order compared to single-part JSON requests.
Orchestrator debug shows pin metadata present in control-plane snapshot but missing in some edge request contexts after normalization transformation.

Correlation discovered: requests with a Content-Disposition filename field are hitting a fast-path in the normalization filter that reserializes headers and drops the 'X-Tenant-Pin' header under a race condition.
Scope estimate: ~1.8% of customer multipart requests in canary cohort; observed only when attachment size between 10KB-200KB and when the upstream connection reuses keep-alive socket.
workaround: Temporarily disable edge normalization canary for Cartograph Labs' tenant (rolled back for their shard) or instruct customers to send attachments via separate upload endpoint and reference the upload token in a pure JSON generation request.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: roll back normalization filter on affected canary shard at 2026-03-12T11:05 UTC for Cartograph Labs. Patch in edge-proxy (fix multipart header preservation) landed in PR 778 and deployed to canary on 2026-03-13 night. Follow-up: orchestration will include an integration test for multipart header preservation and a probe traffic job to validate pin retention on canary nodes before expanding. Assign follow-up ticket INT-2110 for permanent validation and metrics.
